records.title: EPCOT Food and Wine for Three Adults
records.summary: A shared festival day for three experienced adults with unequal constraints, overlapping interests, and different definitions of a good EPCOT day.
constraints: Protect a motion-sensitive traveler without defining the entire group by what she cannot ride.
Treat the aquarium, food, live entertainment, and atmosphere as real priorities.
Avoid fragmenting the group through constant optimization for individual interests.
Build recovery into a rope-drop-to-close day.

perspectives.name: Harbor
perspectives.excerpt: The group should bend without repeatedly breaking apart. Use brief splits only when they create clear value and an easy reunion.
perspectives.full_text: Harbor protects the shared experience. Different needs can coexist without forcing every person through the same attraction or turning the day into parallel solo trips.

perspectives.name: Bo Ra
perspectives.excerpt: The memorable day is not a completed booth list. It is the dish, musician, animal encounter, or sunset the group keeps talking about.
perspectives.full_text: Bo Ra protects the moments that become shared memory. Festival abundance is useful only when attention remains available for discovery.

pin.title: Bo Ra: do not mistake completion for memory
pin.quote: The memorable day is not a completed booth list.

perspectives.name: Jae
perspectives.excerpt: Pick the booths and experiences that matter. You are not required to finish EPCOT.
perspectives.full_text: Jae removes the false goal of completion. A short list of high-value food, attractions, and entertainment protects both time and appetite.

pin.title: Jae: you are not required to finish EPCOT
pin.quote: Pick the booths and experiences that matter. You are not required to finish EPCOT.

perspectives.name: Min
perspectives.excerpt: Heat, food volume, motion sensitivity, and late-day fatigue are system constraints. Plan for them before they become emergencies.
perspectives.full_text: Min protects the plan from predictable failure: too much food too quickly, inadequate rest, and treating known motion sickness as a negotiable preference.

perspectives.name: Nam
perspectives.excerpt: Let the festival day move between motion, taste, conversation, performance, and stillness instead of repeating one mode until it becomes work.
perspectives.full_text: Nam shapes the day as a sequence of contrasting experiences rather than one long consumption loop.

synthesis.principle: Protect constraints, expand meaningful interests, and preserve the group.
synthesis.summary: Use the opening window for shared ride priorities, give the aquarium real time, taste selectively when festival marketplaces open, and alternate food with entertainment, rest, and pavilion exploration. The synthesis distinguishes constraints from interests and uses each perspective to keep the day both workable and memorable.
lessons: Optimization across people is different from optimization across attractions.
A known physical constraint should be protected without making it the person's identity.
Brief, purposeful separation can strengthen a shared day; constant fragmentation cannot.

records.title: Solo DCA and Oogie Boogie Bash
records.summary: One solo traveler, a full park day, a separately ticketed evening, and several valid definitions of success.

experience.duration: One day plus Oogie Boogie Bash

constraints: Protect enough energy for the separately ticketed evening.
Prioritize Halloween-exclusive experiences rather than only ordinary attraction count.
Preserve room for art, atmosphere, live entertainment, and one unexpected memory.
Use rope-drop efficiency without allowing efficiency to consume the whole day.

perspectives.name: Harbor
perspectives.excerpt: Protect the continuity of the experience. Build enough structure to preserve momentum, then leave recovery paths when the day stops cooperating.
perspectives.full_text: Harbor treats the itinerary as a resilient system. The plan should keep its emotional and practical shape when waits rise, energy falls, or an attraction closes.

pin.title: Harbor: protect the shape of the day
pin.quote: Build enough structure to preserve momentum, then leave recovery paths when the day stops cooperating.

perspectives.name: Bo Ra
perspectives.excerpt: Do not optimize away the parts of the day that make it feel like Halloween. Atmosphere is part of the experience, not filler between rides.
perspectives.full_text: Bo Ra protects the emotional register of the day. Seasonal details, art, performance, and the transition into the party matter because they are what make this trip distinct.

pin.title: Bo Ra: atmosphere is infrastructure
pin.quote: Do not optimize away the parts of the day that make it feel like Halloween.

perspectives.name: Jae
perspectives.excerpt: Decide what actually matters today. Spend your time there, and let the rest of the day sort itself out.
perspectives.full_text: Jae compresses the itinerary to the choices that survive real conditions. Use the morning for scarce access, protect the party, and stop pretending every possible attraction deserves equal weight.

pin.title: Jae: focus on what matters today
pin.quote: Decide what actually matters today. Spend your time there, and let the rest of the day sort itself out.

perspectives.name: Min
perspectives.excerpt: A plan is only useful if it still works after a late start, a closure, a long queue, or an energy drop.
perspectives.full_text: Min stress-tests the plan. The evening ticket, food timing, wristband transition, and recovery blocks are operational constraints rather than decorative suggestions.

perspectives.name: Nam
perspectives.excerpt: Let the day have a beginning, a transition, and an evening that feels earned rather than merely appended.
perspectives.full_text: Nam gives the itinerary a narrative shape: energetic opening, intentional slowdown, seasonal transition, and a distinct nighttime conclusion.

synthesis.principle: Efficiency creates room; the traveler decides what deserves that room.
synthesis.summary: Use rope drop for scarce attractions, slow down before fatigue determines the pace, and reserve the evening for experiences that only exist during Oogie Boogie Bash. The final plan preserves the strongest contribution from each independent perspective instead of averaging them into a generic schedule.
lessons: A separately ticketed evening changes the energy budget for the entire day.
Atmosphere and personal artifacts can be deliberate outcomes.
A short priority list improves resilience more than a fully packed schedule.
